help.lead: A course is a graph: the nodes are what the student sees and does, the edges say what comes next.
help.step1: Insert nodes with the + button on the toolbar or the Insert menu; to choose where one goes, drag its type from the + list onto the graph.
help.step2: Connect nodes by dragging from the circle at the bottom of a node to another node.
help.step3: Click a node to edit its content in the inspector; click an edge to edit its condition.
help.step4: The badge at the top shows errors and warnings; click it to see the list and jump to each one.
help.step5: In the Preview tab, take the course as the student would, with the real AI.
help.step6: Open several courses at once, each in its own tab just below the toolbar: nodes copied in one course (⌘C) paste into another (⌘V).
help.step7: Click the ✦ icon at the right end of the toolbar (⇧⌘A) to ask the AI agent to create, review, translate or fix steps; each change it makes can be undone with ⌘Z.

rule.choice-criteria: must be a map of the name of each option to what it covers
rule.choice-few: a choice needs at least two options
rule.choice-many: a choice takes at most 255 options, got {count}
rule.choice-option-name: the option '{name}' must be a name the edges can compare to: lowercase letters, digits and -
rule.choice-option-text: must be a text saying what the option covers, or null
rule.condition-value: 'value' must be a string, number or boolean
rule.content-short: content is very short ({count} words) for a teaching node
rule.data-unused: stores data no edge and no prompt ever reads — branch on it or use it in a prompt
rule.date-real: must be a real date, found {value}
rule.dynamic-static: dynamic node whose prompt reads no {{STORAGE: key}} — nothing personalises it, consider making it static
rule.edge-from: 'from' points to {value}, which is not a node
rule.edge-to: 'to' points to {value}, which is not a node
rule.endings: several nodes end the course: {nodes} — branches should reunite unless every one of these is a real ending
rule.fallback-not-last: the unconditional edge is not last: the following {count} edge(s) are unreachable
rule.fallback-to-feedback: its unconditional edge leads to {target}, which writes from this very judgement -- that edge is the path taken when no judgement was made, so {target} would have nothing to write from; send the fallback elsewhere
rule.fallbacks: {count} unconditional edges; only the first can ever be taken
rule.field-no-options: a '{type}' field must not have options
rule.field-options: a '{type}' field needs at least two options
rule.field-value-twice: option value '{value}' is used twice in this field
rule.form-assignment: a single text-area and no 'instructions': a writing task needs its assignment -- what to write, how long, and what will be judged
rule.form-empty: a form needs at least one field
rule.form-key-twice: field key '{key}' is used twice in this form
rule.from-bypassed: writes from the judgement of {judge}, but there is a path to it that never passes through {judge}: a student taking that path would reach a node with no judgement to write from
rule.from-id: must be the id of a choice, score or noul node, found {value}
rule.from-judging: writes from the judgement of {judge} but its prompt says '{word}': the level is already settled, and a feedback that judges again can contradict the number that routed the student -- tell it how to write, not what to decide
rule.from-missing: writes from '{from}', which is not a node
rule.from-not-judge: writes from '{from}', which is a {type} node and makes no judgement
rule.group-list: must be a list of at least two conditions
rule.group-only: an '{joiner}' condition must contain only '{joiner}', found {fields}
rule.judge-empty: a judgement node needs at least one question
rule.judge-instructions: the question the AI answers must be a non-empty string
rule.judge-key: must be a name like 'track': lowercase letters, digits and -
rule.judge-key-reserved: '{key}' is what a score node produces for the whole node; name the question after what it judges
rule.judge-key-suffix: cannot end in '{suffix}': the node produces that key on its own
rule.judge-key-twice: '{key}' is used twice in the same node
rule.judge-no-fallback: every outgoing edge is conditional; a judgement the AI could not make leaves the student with nowhere to go — add an unconditional fallback edge last
rule.key-levels: '{key}' runs from 0 to {top}, over the levels of its own question, so comparing it against {value} never holds. For a grade out of 100 give the question 'points' and test {owner}.percent
rule.key-not-upstream: '{key}' is produced by {producer}, which is not on any path to {reader}; this condition can never hold
rule.key-unproduced: condition reads '{key}', which no node produces
rule.lang-is-source: '{lang}' is the source language and must not be repeated here
rule.lang-undeclared: language '{lang}' is not declared in info
rule.localized-entry: each entry must be an object with 'lang' and 'text'
rule.localized-list: {label} must be a non-empty list of {lang, text} objects
rule.no-fallback: every outgoing edge is conditional; a student matching none of them gets stuck — add an unconditional fallback edge last
rule.node-object: each node must be an object
rule.node-prefix: id does not match type '{type}' (expected prefix '{prefix}')
rule.noul-criteria: must say what 'true' and what 'false' cover
rule.noul-criteria-field: '{name}' is not a field here: only 'true' and 'false' are
rule.one-correct: exactly one option must be correct, found {count}
rule.other-languages-list: must be a list (use [] when there are no translations)
rule.points-count: {points} point value(s) for {levels} level(s): there must be exactly one per level, in the same order
rule.points-list: must be a list of numbers, one per level of 'criteria'
rule.points-order: the points do not rise with the levels ({points}): a higher level worth less than a lower one is almost always a typo
rule.question-options: a question needs at least two options
rule.question-value-twice: option value '{value}' is used twice in this question
rule.quiz-empty: a quiz needs at least one question
rule.quiz-key-reserved: 'key' cannot be '{key}' — the quiz already produces it
rule.quiz-key-twice: key '{key}' is used twice in this quiz
rule.schema-string: must be a string (the address of the schema)
rule.score-criteria: must be the levels of the scale, in order, from the low end to the high end
rule.score-level-text: each level must say what it means
rule.score-levels: a scale has between 2 and 10 levels, got {count}
rule.section-undeclared: section {number} is not declared in info.sections
rule.spread-all: the correct answer is option {letter} in every question of {scope} — shuffle the options
rule.spread-most: the correct answer is option {letter} in {hits} of {total} questions of {scope} — spread it out
rule.state-field-name: a field name is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens
rule.state-no-storage: the state reads no {{STORAGE: key}}, so the AI judges the same thing for every student and the node always takes the same edge
rule.state-object: the state the AI judges must be an object of named fields, e.g. {"task": "...", "answer": "{{STORAGE: f1.text}}"}
rule.state-reads-mark: the state field '{name}' reads '{key}', a mark already given: the AI would anchor on it instead of judging for itself -- give the judgement the work and the task, not an earlier verdict
rule.storage-not-upstream: {{STORAGE: {key}}} is produced by {producer}, which the student may not have reached before {node}; the value will be empty
rule.storage-unproduced: {{STORAGE: {key}}} reads a key no node produces
rule.system-prompt-language: does not mention the student's language; add 'Answer in the student's language.'
rule.text-or-list: must be a text, or a list of texts
rule.translations-more: {count} text(s) have no '{lang}' version ({sample} and {more} more)
rule.unknown-field: unknown field '{key}' (the format allows no extra fields)
rule.unreachable: no path from the start node reaches: {nodes} (usually a missing edge into them)
rule.word.question: question
rule.word.title: title
rule.words-crossed: 'max-words' ({max}) is below 'min-words' ({min}): no answer can satisfy both
rule.words-not-counted: a '{type}' field counts no words, so it takes no '{bound}'
rule.words-whole: '{bound}' must be a whole number >= 1, found {value}
